Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: The institutional records office files ordinary paperwork in dated records, assigns document identifiers, indexes named fields, and routes copies through designated channels, preserving account references and validation marks. No intake facts appear in this section; only the filing convention is described.

2) What occurred: The actor opened a dated ticket record from the account file, copied the document body, and reproduced it in several new documents. The actor altered validation fields in each copy so the copies matched the original. The actor indexed the copies under new identifiers while retaining the original account reference. The actor transmitted one copy through a designated delivery channel to a named recipient account, scheduled for first use at the gate point, and suppressed refund and chargeback routing fields to prevent reversal processing.

3) Materials/access observed: A dated original ticket document with a validation field and account reference. Several reproduced documents with altered validation fields and copied account references. A delivery channel used to transmit a copy to a named recipient account. Gate-entry scheduling records. Suppressed refund and chargeback routing fields.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple document identifiers sharing a single original account reference. Identical document bodies with divergent validation field values. A delivery channel entry dated before the gate point, targeting a named recipient. Refund and chargeback routing fields present in the schema but absent in value on the reproduced documents.
